_source: ADR 5.2.2.2.2 — hazard warning label models (API field: labels). A legend mapping model number to meaning/background colour/symbol. This is not the full content of Chapters 5.2/5.3 (placarding and labelling) — only the model dictionary itself, sufficient to explain the field's values.

4.1.class: 4.1 — flammable solids / self-reactive substances / polymerizing substances / solid desensitized explosives

4.2.background: Upper half white, lower half red

4.3.class: 4.3 — substances emitting flammable gases in contact with water

5.2.background: Upper half red, lower half yellow

6.2.symbol: Three crescents superimposed on a circle, black
6.2.note: the lower half may bear the text "INFECTIOUS SUBSTANCE" and details of the notification to the health authority

7B.background: Upper half yellow with white border, lower half white
7B.note: text + TRANSPORT INDEX, two red stripes

7C.background: Upper half yellow with white border, lower half white
7C.note: text + TRANSPORT INDEX, three red stripes

7D.background: Upper half yellow, lower half white
7D.note: text RADIOACTIVE or the UN number

8.symbol: Two test tubes with liquid spilling and attacking a hand and a metal, black
8.background: Upper half white, lower half black with white border

9.symbol: 7 vertical stripes in the upper half, black

9A.symbol: 7 vertical stripes + a group of cells (one damaged, emitting flame), black
9A.note: not used as the large placard on a vehicle/container — model 9 is used there instead

additional_marks.environmentally hazardous substance mark: Diamond, black fish and tree on a white or contrasting background, minimum 100×100mm (5.2.1.8.3)
additional_marks.lithium battery mark: Rectangle/square with a hatched red border, cell group symbol + UN number (5.2.1.9), required where special provision 188 or 400 applies
